extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and practitioners looking for textbooks and resources on category theory
extracted.subtask_description: A bibliographic, chronologically-sorted compilation of textbooks, monographs, course notes, videos, and related resources on category theory, organized by topic and level. Intended as a reference for finding introductions, specialized monographs (topos theory, higher categories), and supplemental materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: This page contains a list of textbooks on category theory, sorted in chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are presented in time order (publication year) within sections; use the chronological ordering to trace historical development and editions/reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into topical and level-based sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources are grouped under headings such as 'Introductory texts', 'Textbooks', 'Basic category theory', 'Topos theory', 'Higher category theory', 'Course notes', 'Videos', 'Relation to philosophy', and 'Further resources and links'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these sections to locate material appropriate to level (introductory vs. advanced) or subtopic (topos theory, higher categories, applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of primary historical references and context
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes historical material and primary sources (e.g., Eilenberg & MacLane 1945, Freudenthal 1937) and a short history/discussion explaining origins and motivations of category theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The history section supplies context for why the subject developed and points to foundational papers and historiography; useful for readers seeking original sources or historical perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic detail and metadata for each entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Most entries list author(s), title, publication venue/series, year, publisher, and often identifiers (DOI, ISBN) and links (pdf, arXiv, publisher webpage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries commonly include reprint information, series/volume numbers, and direct links to PDFs or online records (e.g., tac:tr, arXiv, publisher pages) to facilitate access and citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotations indicating audience or emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Some items are annotated with parenthetical notes about intended audience or emphasis — e.g. '(aimed at computer science)', '(emphasis on monoidal category-theory with an eye towards quantum information via dagger-compact categories)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these annotations to pick resources tailored to particular audiences (computer scientists, physicists) or emphases (categorical semantics, monoidal categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of monographs, textbooks, and specialized treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: The list distinguishes general textbooks/monographs from specialized monographs (e.g., devoted to topos theory, higher category theory) and from 'Basic category theory' listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers can identify whether an item is a general introductory text, a graduate-level monograph, or a specialized research-oriented book by its placement and heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of course notes and lecture materials
rubrics_metrics.description: A section catalogs course notes and lecture notes (with years and links) such as 'Category Theory Lecture Notes (2001)', 'Notes on basic category theory (2007)', and university lecture notes taken by students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course notes are presented as lightweight, often freely-available pedagogical supplements; years and links indicate recency and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of multimedia resources (videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists video series and channels relevant to category theory (e.g., 'The Catsters', YouTube playlists), labeled under 'Videos'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia entries point to informal/visual learning resources and are separated from formal texts and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to further resources and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: The page links to related resources such as 'CatDat – A comprehensive database of categories and their properties' and related nLab pages (journals, theses, lost manuscripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outward links provide pathways to databases, community networks, and other curated lists for deeper exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external identifiers and repository markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries frequently include DOIs, ISBNs, arXiv identifiers, tac:tr references, publisher pages, and PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identifiers assist in locating exact editions, electronic copies, and authoritative bibliographic records; the page favors linking to accessible copies when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision/date metadata and edit history
rubrics_metrics.description: The page displays a 'Last revised' timestamp and links to the page history, edits, and discussion ('Last revised on September 17, 2025 at 13:31:17. See the history of this page for a list of all contributions to it. Edit Discuss Previous revision Changes from previous revision History (2 revisions)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision metadata helps users know how up-to-date the list is and provides transparency about contributions and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing within the nLab ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: The page contains intra-site cross-references (e.g., links to 'internal category in homotopy type theory', 'list of journals publishing category theory', and other related nLab pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references help navigate to topic-specific pages or complementary lists within nLab, forming a networked reference structure.
